case_name: Amnider Kaur And Another vs State Of Punjab And Others

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Amnider Kaur and another (run away couple)

facts_of_case: Run away couple filed petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. seeking direction to respondents to protect their life and liberty, which is alleged to have been threatened by the parents.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage solemnised in contravention of the age mentioned in Section 5(iii) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 is only punishable under Section 18 of the Act but would remain valid and enforceable.
legal_principles.held: In this case, it was held that the question of marriage being illegal or void ab-initio on account of the minority of a Hindu spouse is no longer res-integra.
cited_cases: Seema Devi @ Simran Kaur Vs. State of H.P., (1998) 1 RCR (Crl.) 697 (H.P.)
Gindan and others Vs. Barelal, AIR 1976 M.P.83
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — significance in determining the validity of a marriage

legal_principles.principle: A young girl getting married having reached the age of discretion but not attained majority can be sent in protective custody to a Remand Home against their will.
legal_principles.held: In this case, it was observed that State had collected evidence which showed that the girl was more than 18 years of age, therefore, they are not proposed to take any action in the FIR.
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — significance in determining the appropriate course of action for a young girl

use_for_drafting: drafting petitions for runaway couples seeking protection from parents
advising clients on legal options for marrying at a young age
assisting in drafting applications for custody disputes
